presentingComplaint: Recurrent central chest heaviness for 6 hours, ongoing at rest, associated with sweating and breathlessness.
history: 64-year-old man with known hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidaemia presents with three episodes of retrosternal chest heaviness over the past 6 hours, each lasting 15-20 minutes, the last episode still present on arrival with radiation to the left arm and jaw. Associated diaphoresis, nausea, and mild dyspnea. No relief with rest. Denies similar pain before today, though reports increasing exertional chest tightness over the preceding 2 weeks (crescendo pattern). No fever, no cough. Smoker, 20 pack-years. No prior MI or revascularization. No recent cocaine use.
examination: Anxious, diaphoretic male, mild distress from ongoing chest discomfort. No pallor or cyanosis. JVP not raised. Heart sounds normal, no murmur, no rub. Chest clear, no crackles. No peripheral edema. No calf tenderness. Abdomen soft, non-tender. Peripheral pulses intact and symmetric.
imaging: 12-lead ECG on admission: dynamic 1.5mm horizontal ST depression in leads V4-V6 and I, aVL, with T-wave inversion; resolved partially on repeat ECG after 30 minutes then recurred with pain
Chest X-ray: no cardiomegaly, no pulmonary edema, no pneumothorax
Transthoracic echocardiogram: mild hypokinesis of the antero-lateral wall, LVEF 48%, no pericardial effusion
finalDiagnosis: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) with dynamic ECG changes
citations: Harrison 22e - ST-Elevation and Non-ST-Elevation Acute Coronary Syndromes
AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes 2025

contraindications: Caution with dual antiplatelet therapy and anticoagulation if active bleeding risk or planned urgent CABG

edgeCases: Dynamic ST depression with rising troponin distinguishes NSTEMI from unstable angina (troponin-negative) and from STEMI (no ST elevation/new LBBB present)
